statement: 30 segments of lengths \(1, \sqrt{3}, \sqrt{5}, \sqrt{7}, \sqrt{9}, \ldots, \sqrt{59}\) have been drawn on a blackboard. In each step, two of the segments are deleted and a new segment of length equal to the hypotenuse of the right triangle with legs equal to the two deleted segments is drawn. After 29 steps only one segment remains. Find the possible values of its length.
For what positive integer values of \(x\) is \(x^4 + 6x^3 + 11x^2 + 3x + 31\) a perfect square?

Given in the plane the square \(ABCD\), the square \(A_1B_1C_1D_1\) (smaller than the first), and a quadrilateral \(PQRS\) satisfying the following conditions:
\(\bullet\) \(ABCD\) and \(A_1B_1C_1D_1\) have a common center and respectively parallel sides.
\(\bullet\) \(P, Q, R, S\) belong one to each side of the square \(ABCD\).
\(\bullet\) \(A_1, B_1, C_1, D_1\) belong one to each side of the quadrilateral \(PQRS\).
Prove that \(PQRS\) is a square.

A rectangle is divided into 9 small rectangles by lines parallel to its sides. The four numbers written in four of the small rectangles indicate their areas: the values are \(2, 5, 3, 15\) (placed at specific positions as shown in the figure). Prove that the total area of the rectangle is greater than or equal to 90.
figure_description: A rectangle divided into 9 smaller rectangles by 2 vertical and 2 horizontal lines. Four of the nine cells have their areas labeled (values 2, 5, 3, 15 in specific positions).

statement:
Let \(A\) be an infinite set of points in the plane such that inside each circle there are only finitely many points of \(A\), with the following properties:
\(\bullet\) \((0,0)\) belongs to \(A\).
\(\bullet\) If \((a,b)\) and \((c,d)\) belong to \(A\), then \((a-c, b-d)\) belongs to \(A\).
\(\bullet\) There exists a value \(\alpha\) such that by rotating the set \(A\) with center at \((0,0)\) and angle \(\alpha\), the set \(A\) is obtained again.
Prove that \(\alpha\) must be equal to \(\pm 60^\circ\) or \(\pm 90^\circ\) or \(\pm 120^\circ\) or \(\pm 180^\circ\).

A \(9 \times 9\) board has a number written on each square: all squares in the first row have 1, all squares in the second row have 2, \(\ldots\), all squares in the ninth row have 9. A special rectangle is any rectangle of dimensions \(2 \times 3\), \(3 \times 2\), \(4 \times 5\), or \(5 \times 4\) on the board. The permitted operations are:
\(\bullet\) Simultaneously add 1 to all numbers in a special rectangle.
\(\bullet\) Simultaneously subtract 1 from all numbers in a special rectangle.
Demonstrate that it is possible to achieve, through a succession of permitted operations, that 80 squares have the value 0. What number is left in the remaining square?
